# Mega Menu UX Gap Analysis — Stream 3: Recommended Design for Athletica (Desktop + Mobile)

> **Compiled by:** Probe-Beacon (Intelligence Team Member)
> **Task:** stream-3-mega-menu-ux-gap-analysis
> **Date:** 2026-07-19
> **Purpose:** Synthesize existing research (6 parts, 41 sources) into a comprehensive design recommendation for Athletica's mega menu navigation, covering Desktop (Part A), Mobile (Part B), Accessibility (Part C), and Unresolved Items (Part D).
> **Sources:** mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md through part6.md; current implementation at MegaMenu.tsx, navigation.json

---

## PART A: Desktop Design

### A1. 4-Column Layout Recommendation

Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: "For Athletica's 5-level hierarchy: 4 columns." Backed by NN/g chunking guidance, Baymard's ~10 items max, and Boundev's multi-column recommendation. Also per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 wireframe.

#### Column 1 — Category Edits (Level 1)

**Content:**
- **"All [Category]"** as clickable heading → full category page (e.g., "All Boots")
- **Curated Edits:** New In, Best Sellers, By Surface (FG, AG, TF, SG)
- **By Surface** is Athletica-specific — a unique differentiator for football boots

**Inspiration:**
- JD Sports' "Edits" column — Column 1 in their 6-column template (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: "Column 1: 'Edits' (curated collections: New In, Summer Edit, Holiday Shop)")
- Nike's "New & Featured" column — Column 1 in their 3-5 column layout (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: "Column 1: 'New & Featured' (curated links: New Releases, Best Sellers, Latest Drops)")

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Curated 'Edits': New In, Best Sellers, By Surface (FG, AG, TF, SG)"
- mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: JD Sports "Edits" column pattern
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: Nike "New & Featured" column

#### Column 2 — Brands with 48px Logos (Level 2)

**Content:**
- Each brand with a small logo (48×48px) before the brand name
- Brands list: Nike, Adidas, Puma, New Balance, Mizuno, Umbro, etc.
- Brand names as clickable links → brand category page (e.g., `/boots/nike/`)

**Inspiration:**
- Foot Locker's "Brands" column (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.4: "Each mega menu panel includes a dedicated 'Brands' column listing top brands. Directly relevant to Athletica's Level 2 (Brand)")
- JD Sports' brand column (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: "Column 5: Brands (Nike, adidas, New Balance, etc.)")

**Logo size:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: "Small brand logos (48×48px) next to Level 2 brand names in Column 2"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Each brand with a small logo (48×48px)"

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.4: Foot Locker brand column
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: 48px logo size guidance
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Column 2 wireframe

#### Column 3 — Models with 60px Thumbnails (Level 3)

**Content:**
- Each model with a small product thumbnail (60×60px)
- Top models grouped by brand (e.g., Nike: Mercurial, Phantom, Tiempo, Zoom)
- Model names as clickable links → model PLP (e.g., `/boots/nike/mercurial/`)
- Vertical scroll if model list exceeds available viewport height
- No horizontal scrolling

**Thumbnail size:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: "Small product thumbnails (60×60px) next to Level 3 model names in Column 3"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Thumbnails at 60px per Probe-Sable (Part A, §A4)"

**Scrolling behavior:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Vertical scroll if model list exceeds available space"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.6: "Mega menu panel scrolls vertically if content exceeds viewport height"

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: 60px thumbnail guidance
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Column 3 wireframe
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Scrolling behavior

#### Column 4 — Featured/Promotional (Single CTA)

**Content:**
- Single promotional image (latest release spotlight)
- "Shop All [Category]" or "Shop Now" CTA button below image
- Single image only — no carousel, auto-play, or complex widgets

**Inspiration:**
- JD Sports' `nav-promotions` section (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: "Each mega menu panel has a right-side promotion column with a large product/category image and a CTA link")
- Nike's promotional image block (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: "Promotional image on the right side — optional one-column-wide promotional banner")

**Anti-pattern warning:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.7: "Avoid carousels, accordions within the menu, or interactive filtering. The mega menu should be a navigation tool, not a full-featured page." (NN/g)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Single image only — no carousel, auto-play, or complex widgets"

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: JD Sports promo column
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: Nike promo image block
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.7: No GUI widgets warning

#### Bottom Row Design

**Content:**
- "View All [Category]" link (left-aligned) — inspired by Adidas's bold "All" links
- "View All Brands" link (right-aligned) — links to full brand directory
- Full-width row with subtle visual separator (border-top or background tint)

**Inspiration:**
- Adidas's bold "All" links (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2: "'All' category links in bold — Bold 'All' links at the bottom of each submenu")
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.6: "Persistent 'View All [Category]' link (inspired by Adidas's bold 'All' links per econsultancy.com)"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Bottom row: 'View All Boots' (left) — inspired by Adidas's bold 'All' links... 'View All Brands' (right)"

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2: Adidas bottom row
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.6: View All link pattern
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Bottom row wireframe

---

### A2. Top-Level Nav Reduction Strategy

**Research recommendation: Max 6 top-level items**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: NN/g recommends chunking into "related sets" with medium granularity
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.8 comparison table: Nike has ~6, Adidas ~5, Foot Locker 7, JD Sports 7

**Current navigation.json has 11 top-level categories:**
1. Boots
2. Multi-Stud Boots
3. Indoor Shoes
4. Shin Guards
5. Balls
6. Socks
7. Jerseys
8. Kits
9. Apparel
10. Clothing
11. Accessories

_(Source: navigation.json Level 1 items identified from file reading — items with `"level": 1`)_

**Proposed consolidation to 6 top-level items:**

| Top-Level Item | Includes |
|---|---|
| **Boots** | Boots + Multi-Stud Boots + Indoor Shoes (merge all footwear categories) |
| **Jerseys/Kits** | Jerseys + Kits (merge match kit categories) |
| **Clothing** | Clothing + Apparel (merge training/casual apparel) |
| **Accessories** | Accessories + Shin Guards + Socks + Balls (merge accessories categories) |
| **Brands** | Brand directory (A–Z brand browsing, inspired by ASOS) |
| **Sale** | Promotional/discounted items |

**Strategy rationale:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: "Max 6 top-level items" — research from NN/g, Baymard
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Level 1 categories as text links: Boots | Clothing | Equipment | Accessories | Brands | Sale"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 (footnote): "Nike's ~6-item top-level nav (per styles.refero.design); JD Sports' consistent template"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.8: Cross-site comparison shows industry leaders operate with 5-7 top-level items

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: Max 6 items guidance
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Top-level nav proposal
- mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.8: Comparison tables

---

### A3. Hover/Click Behavior Design

**Primary: Click-to-Open**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Use Click-Activated (Rather Than Hover-Activated) Submenus" (NN/g guideline #13, 2024)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: Boundev (2026): "We never use hover-triggered mega menus in new projects. Click activation is more precise"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Primary: Click to open — consistent across devices"

**Secondary: Hover with 400ms delay**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Hover with 400ms delay + Amazon triangle technique for mouse users who prefer it"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Secondary: Hover with 400ms delay — for mouse users (per Baymard 300-500ms recommendation)"

**Amazon triangle technique (trajectory forgiveness):**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Use the 'Amazon triangle' technique (trajectory triangle connecting mouse pointer position to mega menu edges) to prevent accidental closes when moving diagonally toward submenu items" (Source: bjk5.com)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Amazon triangle technique — trajectory triangle prevents accidental closes during diagonal movement"

**Exit delay: 500ms minimum**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Exit delay: 500ms minimum before menu closes on mouse leave" (Source: NN/g, "Mega Menus Work Well", 2017)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Exit delay: 500ms minimum before menu closes"

**Close behaviors:**
- Click outside panel → close
- Escape key → close
- Clicking a navigation link → navigate + close
- Mouse leave for 500ms → close (with triangle forgiveness)

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: Full hover/click specification
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Hover/click behavior

---

### A4. Level Cutoff Design

**Show 3 levels in mega menu (L1-L3):**

| Mega Menu Level | Category Level | Example | Handled By |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-level nav bar | Level 1: Category | "Boots" | Mega menu text link |
| Column 2 (Brands) | Level 2: Brand | "Nike", "Adidas" | Mega menu with 48px logos |
| Column 3 (Models) | Level 3: Model | "Mercurial", "Phantom" | Mega menu with 60px thumbs |
| PLP Filters | Level 4: Sub-model | "Vapor 16 Elite" | PLP faceted filters |
| PLP Filters | Level 5: Product Type | "FG", "AG", "TF" | PLP filter chips |

**Cutoff rationale:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.5: "Mega menu shows Levels 1–3 (Category → Brand → Model). Each Level 3 link → intermediary category PLP"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.2: NN/g: "can support 2–3 tiers of information reasonably well" and recommends sending users to "routing pages with additional options"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.2: "Levels 1-3 in mega menu — NN/g: mega menus 'can support 2–3 tiers'"

**PLP handling for L4-L5:**
- Level 4 sub-models as filterable category groups with thumbnails on PLP
- Level 5 (Product Type) as filter facets (checkbox or button group)
- PLP breadcrumbs show full path: `Boots > Nike > Mercurial > Vapor 16 Elite > FG`
- Left sidebar on PLP showing sibling sub-models and parent categories

**PLP sidebar inspiration:**
- Nike's nested left-hand sidebar (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: "Nike adds a nested left-hand sidebar menu above the filters showing the current category hierarchy")
- Decathlon's "Activities" sidebar (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.3: "Category landing page with a sidebar 'Activities' navigation showing sibling/subsidiary categories")

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.5: Cutoff point
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.2: Hierarchy mapping
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: Nike sidebar
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.3: Decathlon sidebar

---

### A5. Bottom Row Design

**Design specification:**
- Full-width row at the bottom of the mega menu panel
- Subtle visual separator (1px border-top, e.g., `border-gray-800`)
- Left: "View All [Category]" link (e.g., "View All Boots →")
- Right: "View All Brands →" link → brand directory page
- Both links in bold, uppercase, with arrow indicator
- Hover state: primary/accent color change

**Inspiration:**
- Adidas's distinctive bottom row (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2: "Full-width bottom section with additional links, 'View All' options")
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Full-width, subtle visual separator"

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2: Adidas bottom row
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: Bottom row specification

---

## PART B: Mobile Design

### B1. Hybrid Accordion + Drill-Down Design

**Primary recommendation:** Hybrid accordion (L1→L2) + drill-down (L2→L3+)

**Pattern switch point:** Level 2

Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1:
- **Level 1 → Level 2:** Accordion inside full-screen overlay. Tapping a Level 1 category expands inline to show Level 2 brands
- **Level 2 → Level 3+:** Push/drill-down navigation. Tapping a Level 2 brand triggers a push transition to a new full-screen panel

**NN/g decision algorithm (per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1):**
- <6 subcategories → accordion/submenu
- 6–15 subcategories → section menu
- 15+ → category landing page

Athletica's Level 1→2 (Category→Brand) typically has 5-10 brands — falls in accordion sweet spot. Level 2→3 (Brand→Model) may exceed 6 items, justifying switch to drill-down.

**Why hybrid works for 5 levels (per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.2):**
- Levels 1–2 (Accordion): Users see all top-level categories at a glance. Supports "sideways browsing" — jumping between brands
- Levels 3–5 (Drill-down): Full-screen focus on branch. Avoids "nested doll navigation" problem (NN/g term)
- Hybrid switch at Level 2 prevents accordion from pushing content too far down the screen (SGS case study)

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1: Hybrid pattern recommendation
- mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.2: Why this works for 5 levels
- mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.3: Athletica mobile structure

---

### B2. Full-Screen Overlay Design

**Overlay characteristics:**
- Hamburger icon opens a full-screen overlay (inspired by Nike per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1)
- Left-side slide-in drawer that takes over the full viewport
- Do NOT use partial overlay — users need full screen for deep hierarchy

**Persistent search bar:**
- At the top of the mobile nav overlay
- Inspired by Decathlon's search-first approach (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.3: "Search is prominently positioned at the top — reflects search-first philosophy")
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5: "Persistent at the top of the mobile nav overlay (inspired by Decathlon's search-first approach per hmmh.de case study)"

**"View All" links at every level:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5: "Every level should have a prominent 'View All [Category]' link at the bottom"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1: "At any level: A 'View All [Category]' link and a prominent 'Back' button"
- Source: Baymard — "only 24% get it right"

**Touch targets: 44×44px minimum**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: "Minimum 44×44px, ideally 48×48dp (Material Design 3)"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: "Minimum 44×44px for all clickable items"

**Animations:**
- **Accordion:** Staggered fade-in (~50ms per item) — Nike-style (per muffingroup.com, mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)
- **Drill-down:** CSS transform slide (200–300ms) — per SGS case study (mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)

**Icons:**
- Chevron-right (→) for drill-down items (Level 3+)
- Chevron-down (▼) for accordion expand (Level 1→2)
- Keep icons consistent (per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)

**Performance:**
- Load L1–L3 in HTML by default
- Conditionally load deeper branches via JavaScript on user intent
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5: SGS case study loaded first 3 levels in HTML, deeper via JS

**Source citations:**

## PART C: Accessibility & Edge Cases

### C1. WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance

Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8 and mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7:

**Keyboard Navigation:**
- Tab / Shift+Tab: Navigate between top-level items and within menu
- Enter / Space: Open/activate submenus and links
- Arrow keys: Navigate within submenus (Up/Down for vertical, Left/Right for columns)
- Escape: Close menu and return focus to trigger
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: "Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance required"

**ARIA Attributes:**
- `aria-expanded` (true/false) on parent items to indicate menu state
- `aria-haspopup="menu"` on menu triggers
- `role="navigation"` on main nav landmark
- `aria-current="page"` for active category
- `aria-controls` linking trigger to panel ID
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: Boundev (2026) recommendation

**Focus Management:**
- When drill-down pushes a new screen on mobile: move focus to panel heading
- On close: return focus to the trigger element (hamburger or top-level link)
- Visible focus indicators on all navigable elements (at minimum a 2px outline)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: "On drill-down push, move focus to panel heading. On close, return focus to trigger"

**Contrast Requirements:**
- All text: WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text
- Large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold): 3:1 minimum
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8

**Touch Targets:**
- Minimum 44×44px for all clickable items
- Indentation for hierarchy: 16–20px per level
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: NN/g and Material Design 3

**prefers-reduced-motion:**
- Disable slide animations when user prefers reduced motion
- Accordion: fade without stagger animation
- Drill-down: instant swap (no slide transition)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: WCAG 2.1 — 2.3.3

**Screen Reader Support:**
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: Two approaches recommended by NN/g:
  - Simple: Each top-level menu choice clickable → regular page with accessible HTML
  - Advanced: Full ARIA implementation with keyboard handlers
  - Ideally implement both approaches

**Orientation Support:**
- Support both portrait and landscape layouts
- In landscape: consider split-menu showing two levels side-by-side
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: Smashing Magazine (2022)

**Back Button Behavior:**
- Use breadcrumb-style back ("← Back to [Parent]"), not generic "Back"
- Avoid confusion with browser back button
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: NN/g, "Mobile Subnavigation", 2017

**Source citations:**
- mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: Desktop accessibility
- mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: Mobile accessibility

# Mega Menu UX Gap Analysis — Stream 3: Recommended Design (Part A: Desktop + Part B: Mobile)

> **Compiled by:** Probe-Beacon (Intelligence Team Member)
> **Task:** stream-3-mega-menu-ux-gap-analysis
> **Date:** 2026-07-19
> **Sources:** mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md through part6.md; current MegaMenu.tsx, navigation.json

---

## PART A: Desktop Design

### A1. 4-Column Layout Recommendation

Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: "For Athletica's 5-level hierarchy: 4 columns." Backed by NN/g chunking, Baymard (~10 items max), and Boundev multi-column recommendation. Also per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 wireframe.

### Column 1 — Category Edits (Level 1)
- **"All [Category]"** clickable heading → full category page
- **Curated Edits:** New In, Best Sellers, By Surface (FG, AG, TF, SG)
- **By Surface** is Athletica-specific differentiator for football boots
- **Inspiration:** JD Sports' "Edits" column (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5: "Column 1: Edits (curated collections: New In, Summer Edit, Holiday Shop)")
- **Inspiration:** Nike's "New & Featured" column (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1: "Column 1: New & Featured (curated links: New Releases, Best Sellers, Latest Drops)")
- **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Curated 'Edits': New In, Best Sellers, By Surface"

### Column 2 — Brands with 48px Logos (Level 2)
- Each brand with small logo (48×48px) before brand name
- Brands list: Nike, Adidas, Puma, New Balance, Mizuno, Umbro, etc.
- Brand names as clickable links → brand category page
- **Inspiration:** Foot Locker's "Brands" column (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.4: "Each mega menu panel includes a dedicated 'Brands' column listing top brands")
- **Logo size:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: "Small brand logos (48×48px)"
- **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Each brand with a small logo (48×48px)"

### Column 3 — Models with 60px Thumbnails (Level 3)
- Each model with small product thumbnail (60×60px)
- Top models grouped by brand (Nike: Mercurial, Phantom, Tiempo, Zoom)
- Model names as clickable links → model PLP
- Vertical scroll if model list exceeds viewport height (no horizontal scroll)
- **Thumbnail size:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.4: "Small product thumbnails (60×60px)"
- **Scrolling:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Vertical scroll if model list exceeds available space"
- **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 Column 3 wireframe

### Column 4 — Featured/Promotional (Single CTA)
- Single promotional image (latest release spotlight)
- "Shop All [Category]" or "Shop Now" CTA button
- **Single image only** — no carousel, auto-play, or complex widgets
- **Anti-pattern:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.7: "Avoid carousels, accordions within the menu"
- **Inspiration:** JD Sports' `nav-promotions` (per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5); Nike's promo image block (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1)
- **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Single image only — no carousel, auto-play, or complex widgets"

### Bottom Row Design
- "View All [Category]" (left-aligned) | "View All Brands" (right-aligned)
- Full-width row with subtle visual separator (border-top)
- **Inspiration:** Adidas's bold "All" links (per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2)
- **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 bottom row

---

### A2. Top-Level Nav Reduction Strategy

**Current: 11 items in navigation.json:** Boots, Multi-Stud Boots, Indoor Shoes, Shin Guards, Balls, Socks, Jerseys, Kits, Apparel, Clothing, Accessories

**Research says max 6 top-level items** (per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1: NN/g chunking guidance). Per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.8: Nike ~6, Adidas ~5, Foot Locker 7, JD Sports 7.

**Proposed consolidation to 6:**

| Top-Level Item | Includes From Current |
|---|---|
| **Boots** | Boots + Multi-Stud Boots + Indoor Shoes |
| **Jerseys/Kits** | Jerseys + Kits |
| **Clothing** | Clothing + Apparel |
| **Accessories** | Accessories + Shin Guards + Socks + Balls |
| **Brands** | Brand directory (A–Z) |
| **Sale** | Promotional/discounted items |

**Strategy rationale:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Level 1 categories as text links: Boots | Clothing | Equipment | Accessories | Brands | Sale". Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Nike's ~6-item top-level nav (per styles.refero.design); JD Sports' consistent template"

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.1, mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1

---

### A3. Hover/Click Behavior Design

**Primary: Click-to-open** — consistent across devices.
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Use Click-Activated (Rather Than Hover-Activated) Submenus" (NN/g guideline #13, 2024)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: Boundev (2026): "Click activation is more precise"

**Secondary: Hover with 400ms delay** for mouse users.
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: "Hover with 400ms delay + Amazon triangle technique"
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1: "Secondary: Hover with 400ms delay"

**Amazon triangle technique** — trajectory triangle prevents accidental closes during diagonal movement toward submenu items.
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: Source: bjk5.com

**Exit delay: 500ms minimum** before menu closes on mouse leave.
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3: Source: NN/g, "Mega Menus Work Well", 2017

**Close behaviors:** Click outside panel, Escape key, or clicking a nav link

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.3, mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1

---

### A4. Level Cutoff Design

**Mega menu shows Levels 1-3 only.** Levels 4-5 deferred to PLP.

| Mega Menu | Level | Example | Handled By |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-level nav bar | L1: Category | "Boots" | Menu text link |
| Column 2 | L2: Brand | "Nike" | Menu with 48px logos |
| Column 3 | L3: Model | "Mercurial" | Menu with 60px thumbs |
| PLP Filters | L4: Sub-model | "Vapor 16 Elite" | PLP faceted filters |
| PLP Filters | L5: Product Type | "FG, AG, TF" | PLP filter chips |

**Cutoff rationale:** Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.5: NN/g: mega menus "can support 2–3 tiers" and recommends routing pages for deeper levels. Per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.2: "Levels 1-3 in mega menu — NN/g: 'can support 2–3 tiers'"

**PLP handling for L4-L5:**
- L4 sub-models as filterable category groups with thumbnails
- L5 Product Type as filter facets (checkbox/button group)
- Breadcrumbs on PLP: `Boots > Nike > Mercurial > Vapor 16 Elite > FG`
- Left sidebar on PLP showing sibling sub-models (inspired by Nike's nested sidebar per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1; Decathlon's "Activities" sidebar per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.3)

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.5, mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.2

---

### A5. Bottom Row Design Details
- Full-width row at bottom of mega menu panel
- Subtle visual separator (1px border-top)
- Left: "View All [Category] →" link
- Right: "View All Brands →" link
- Bold, uppercase, with arrow indicator
- Hover state: accent color change

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2 (Adidas); mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1

---

## PART B: Mobile Design

### B1. Hybrid Accordion + Drill-Down Design

**Pattern:** Hybrid accordion (L1→L2) + drill-down/push navigation (L2→L3+).

Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1:
- **Level 1 → Level 2:** Accordion inside full-screen overlay. Tapping L1 expands inline to show L2 brands
- **Level 2 → Level 3+:** Push transition to new full-screen panel. Each tap pushes a new screen.

**Switch point at Level 2** per NN/g decision algorithm (mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1):
- <6 subcategories → accordion/submenu
- 6–15 → section menu
- 15+ → category landing page

**Why hybrid works:**
- Levels 1–2 (Accordion): Users see all top-level categories at once, supports "sideways browsing"
- Levels 3–5 (Drill-down): Full-screen focus on branch. Avoids "nested doll navigation" (NN/g term)
- Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.2: Accordions fail at depth because expanded ancestors push content too far down

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.1-3.2, mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.3

---

### B2. Full-Screen Overlay Design

**Overlay:** Hamburger icon → full-screen overlay (left-side slide-in drawer). Nike-style per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1.

**Persistent search bar** at top of overlay (Decathlon's search-first per mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.3).

**"View All" links at every level** — per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5: Baymard: "only 24% get it right", high-impact low-effort.

**Touch targets:** 44×44px minimum (per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7, NN/g; Material Design 3).

**Animations:**
- **Accordion:** Staggered fade-in ~50ms per item (Nike-style per muffingroup.com, mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)
- **Drill-down:** CSS transform slide, 200–300ms (SGS case study per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)

**Icons:** Chevron-right (→) for drill-down items (L3+), chevron-down (▼) for accordion expand (L1→L2)

**Performance:** Load L1–L3 in HTML by default, lazy-load deeper branches via JS on intent (SGS case study per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5)

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5, §3.7

**Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.3 wireframes, mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.4 diagrams

## Current Implementation Analysis (MegaMenu.tsx)

**Gaps between current code and recommended design:**

1. **Column structure is algorithmic** — current `buildColumns()` creates dynamic columns based on L2/L3/L4 counts. Recommended design proposes fixed 4-column layout with specific roles.

2. **Missing Column 1 (Edits)** — current shows L2-L4 items only. No curated "Edits" column.

3. **No bottom row** — no "View All [Category]" or "View All Brands" links.

4. **No brand logos or product thumbnails** — text-only. Recommended has 48px logos (C2) and 60px thumbs (C3).

5. **No hover/click differentiation** — no 400ms delay, Amazon triangle, or 500ms exit delay.

6. **Right sidebar is "Quick Links"** — current has Track Order/Authenticity/Pro Support. Recommended replaces with Column 4 featured promotional content.

7. **No level cutoff** — current attempts L2-L4 in menu with complex batching. Recommended shows L1-L3 only.

# Mega Menu UX Gap Analysis — Stream 3: Recommended Design (Part C: Accessibility + Part D: Unresolved Items) > **Compiled by:** Probe-Beacon (Intelligence Team Member) > **Task:** stream-3-mega-menu-ux-gap-analysis > **Date:** 2026-07-19 > **Sources:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8, part4.md §3.7, part6.md §4.5 --- ## PART C: Accessibility & Edge Cases ### C1. Keyboard Navigation (Full WCAG 2.1 AA) Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8 and mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: | Key | Desktop Behavior | Mobile Behavior | |---|---|---| | **Tab / Shift+Tab** | Navigate between top-level nav items; move into panel | Navigate through overlay items | | **Enter / Space** | Open submenu or activate link | Open accordion or drill-down | | **Up/Down Arrow** | Navigate within submenu items | Navigate within current level list | | **Left/Right Arrow** | Switch between columns | N/A (mobile is single-column) | | **Escape** | Close menu, return focus to trigger | Close overlay, return focus to hamburger | **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: "Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance required. Tab/Shift+Tab between top-level items, Enter/Space to open submenus, Arrow keys within submenus, Escape to close." ### C2. ARIA Attributes | Attribute | Applied To | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `aria-expanded="true/false"` | Top-level nav items, accordion parents | Indicates menu/open state | | `aria-haspopup="menu"` | Menu triggers | Announces presence of submenu to screen readers | | `role="navigation"` | Main nav `
` element | Landmark identification | | `aria-current="page"` | Active link | Indicates current category | | `aria-controls="panel-id"` | Trigger element | Links trigger to its panel | **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8: Boundev (2026) recommendation; NN/g "Mega Menus Work Well" (2017) ### C3. Focus Management - **Desktop:** When mega menu opens, move focus to first link in Column 1. When closes, return focus to the top-level trigger. - **Mobile drill-down:** On push transition, move focus to the new panel heading (e.g., `

Nike Models

`). On back/close, return focus to the item that was activated. - **Visible focus indicators** on all navigable elements — minimum 2px outline with sufficient contrast. - **Skip link** before navigation for keyboard users to bypass the menu entirely. **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: "On drill-down push, move focus to panel heading. On close, return focus to trigger." (WCAG 2.1 — 2.4.3) ### C4. Touch Targets - **Minimum:** 44×44px for all clickable items (per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8) - **Ideal:** 48×48dp (Material Design 3 standard, per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7) - **Hierarchy indentation:** 16–20px per level on mobile (per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.5) - **Spacing between items:** Minimum 8px gap to prevent accidental taps ### C5. prefers-reduced-motion Support When user has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` preference: - **Accordion animations:** Disable staggered fade. Items appear instantly (no transition). - **Drill-down transitions:** Disable slide animation. New panel appears instantly (CSS transform disabled). - **Hover effects:** Disable transition timing — instant visual change instead. - **Implementation:** Use `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` in CSS to override animation durations to 0ms. Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: "Provide `prefers-reduced-motion` support — disable slide animations." (WCAG 2.1 — 2.3.3) ### C6. Screen Reader Support Per mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8, NN/g recommends two approaches: **Simple approach:** Make each top-level menu choice clickable → regular category page with full accessible HTML. Users can navigate without the mega menu JavaScript. **Advanced approach:** Full ARIA implementation with: - Proper `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"` roles - Keyboard event handlers for all interactions - `aria-live="polite"` for dynamic content updates - Focus trapping within open menus **Recommendation:** Implement both. "If you're a rich company and/or especially concerned with accessibility, you should implement both." — NN/g ### C7. Color Contrast - **Normal text:** WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio - **Large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold):** 3:1 minimum - **Focus indicators:** 3:1 against adjacent background - **Hover states:** Maintain sufficient contrast — color-only changes must be supplemented with another indicator (underline, weight change) **Source:** mega-menu-ux-research-part3.md §2.8 ### C8. Edge Cases **Very long brand lists (Column 2):** - Maximum height: cap at viewport height minus nav bar height minus bottom row (approximately 60vh) - Vertical scroll if content exceeds max height - With "View All Brands" at bottom to see complete list **Very long model lists (Column 3):** - Same vertical scroll treatment - Sort by popularity/sales — most relevant models first **No JavaScript fallback:** - If JS fails to load, top-level nav items should link directly to category pages - Mega menu enhancement: progressive enhancement - Per NN/g recommendation: simple clickable links as baseline **Orientation change (mobile):** - Support both portrait and landscape - In landscape, consider showing two levels (breadcrumb + current level) side-by-side - Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: Smashing Magazine (2022) **Back button behavior:** - Use breadcrumb-style "← Back to [Parent]" labels, not generic "Back" - Navigation back stack independent of browser history - Per mega-menu-ux-research-part4.md §3.7: NN/g "Mobile Subnavigation" (2017) --- ## PART D: Unresolved Items [NOT FOUND — ask CEO] The following 7 items require CEO/Product Owner input. Source: mega-menu-ux-research-part6.md §4.5. ### D1. Audience Segmentation (Gender-first or Category-first?) **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Should top-level nav split by Gender (Men's/Women's/Kids') or by Category (Boots/Clothing/Accessories)? **Context:** - Nike: audience-first (Men/Women/Kids) — mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.1 - JD Sports: category-first — mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.5 - Zalando: stores gender in cookie `ncx` — mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.7 - Current navigation.json uses "Adultos" as Level 0 (category-first approach) **Options for CEO:** - A: Category-first (Boots | Jerseys/Kits | Clothing | Accessories | Brands | Sale) — simpler, fewer clicks - B: Gender-first (Men | Women | Kids) then categories — deeper but audience-specific - C: Hybrid (category-first with audience filter on PLP) ### D2. Exact Category Taxonomy **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Confirm exact Level 1 categories for final taxonomy. **Current 11 items:** Boots, Multi-Stud Boots, Indoor Shoes, Shin Guards, Balls, Socks, Jerseys, Kits, Apparel, Clothing, Accessories **Research proposes 6:** Boots | Jerseys/Kits | Clothing | Accessories | Brands | Sale **CEO needs to decide:** - Whether Boots + Multi-Stud Boots + Indoor Shoes merge into "Boots" - Whether Jerseys + Kits merge into "Kits" (or "Jerseys") - Whether Clothing + Apparel merge into "Clothing" - Whether Accessories + Shin Guards + Socks + Balls merge into "Accessories" - Whether "Equipment" should be a separate category (per mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1) - Whether "Sale" should be top-level or within a "More" dropdown ### D3. Surface Types **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Is "By Surface" (FG/AG/TF/SG) the correct second-dimension filter? **Context:** - "By Surface" proposed as Athletica differentiator — mega-menu-ux-research-part5.md §4.1 - Current nav has "Surface" as L2 under Boots: Natural Grass, Artificial Turf, Hard Ground/Dirt - Adidas uses "Sport" as second dimension — mega-menu-ux-research-part1.md §1.2 **CEO needs to decide:** - Surface options: FG, AG, TF, SG — correct four? - Should "By Player Position" or "By Skill Level" be additional dimensions? - "By Surface" or "By Sport" as second dimension? ### D4. Brand List **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Which brands does Athletica carry? Affects Column 2 brand listing. **Current brands observed in nav data:** Nike, Adidas, Puma, New Balance, Mizuno, Joma, Kelme, Lotto, Munich, Diadora **CEO needs to provide:** - Complete brand list for Column 2 - Priority ordering (which brands at top) - Whether all brands have 48px logo assets ### D5. Mobile Search Persistence **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Should search bar remain visible in header after hamburger menu opens? **Options:** - A: Search in header (visible above menu icon) — Nike pattern - B: Search at top of overlay (inside menu) — Decathlon pattern - C: Both ### D6. Cookie-Based Personalization **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Implement cookie-based preference to skip re-selection for returning visitors? **Context:** Zalando stores gender in `ncx` cookie per mega-menu-ux-research-part2.md §1.7. Applies Hick's Law. **CEO needs to decide:** - Whether to implement cookie personalization - GDPR/compliance implications - What preferences to store (gender? surface? favorite brand?) ### D7. Promotional Column Ownership **[NOT FOUND — ask CEO]** **Question:** Who manages Column 4 promotional content? **Context:** Column 4 requires fresh content to stay relevant. If no resources, column risks becoming stale. **CEO needs to decide:** - Owning team (Marketing? Operations? Product?) - Update frequency (weekly? per launch?) - Fallback content when no promo available - CMS-managed dynamic content or static? --- ## Summary: Key Design Decisions | Decision | Recommendation | Primary Source | |---|---|---| | **Column layout** | 4 columns (Edits, Brands, Models, Promo) | Part 3 §2.1, Part 5 §4.1 | | **Top-level items** | 6 max (consolidate from 11) | Part 3 §2.1, Part 5 §4.1 | | **Hover/Click** | Click primary, hover secondary (400ms delay) | Part 3 §2.3, Part 5 §4.1 | | **Exit delay** | 500ms minimum | Part 3 §2.3 | | **Levels shown** | L1-L3 in menu, L4-L5 on PLP | Part 3 §2.5, Part 5 §4.2 | | **Images** | 48px brand logos + 60px product thumbs | Part 3 §2.4 | | **Bottom row** | View All [Category] + View All Brands | Part 1 §1.2, Part 5 §4.1 | | **Mobile pattern** | Hybrid accordion (L1-L2) + drill-down (L3+) | Part 4 §3.1, Part 5 §4.3 | | **Touch targets** | 44×44px minimum | Part 3 §2.8, Part 4 §3.7 | | **Animations** | Staggered fade 50ms/item (accordion), 200-300ms slide (push) | Part 4 §3.5 | | **Unresolved** | 7 items — need CEO input | Part 6 §4.5 |
